# kenji: the metrics he chose

## What he asked for

1. **A slope with an interval on it.** Not a direction, not a verdict. He will
   accept "cannot say" cheerfully and considers it the honest answer more
   often than the engine does.
2. **The detection horizon.** How many more mornings until the slope he is
   looking at separates from zero at his own stated confidence. This is the
   metric the schema cannot express, and it is the one he actually checks.

## What he declined

**A daily verdict.** He regards rendering a single morning's reading as a
statement about his body as the same error as reporting a single measurement
without its uncertainty, and he says so.

**A smoothed line.** He wants the readings and the interval, not a curve drawn
through them, on the grounds that a smoother hides exactly the scatter he is
trying to characterise.

## What this record is NOT representative of

**His logging is not typical and must not be read as if it were.** He records
both energy figures on every one of 175 days. The real record this engine was
built for logged intake on 24 per cent of days, and those the days eating went
to plan (#372).

He logs completely because the experiment has an end date and he treats it as
one. `WORLD.md` says what he does after it ends: he stops weighing his food
the same week, and keeps the morning weigh-in.
